name: Laos
sources: GDP $865.6m and population 4.312m (World Bank, 1990). The smallest economy on the roster.
CPI inflation 35.6% (World Bank, 1990) — the price level finding itself as the New Economic Mechanism, adopted in 1986, removed state pricing and let the kip float.

interest_rate 0.35 is entered against that inflation to hold the real rate near zero. The Bank of the Lao PDR was still being separated from the commercial banking function in 1990 and published no policy rate; this is a construction, not a transcription, and it is flagged as one.

No World Bank or SIPRI military expenditure figure exists for Laos in 1990. 4.5% of GDP is an estimate consistent with a 55,000-strong army in a country of four million and with the Vietnamese divisions still stationed there.

External debt near 1.7x GDP, overwhelmingly non-convertible ruble obligations to the Soviet Union. The dollar value of that debt was disputed until it was written down in the 1990s, which is why the ratio looks worse than the country's actual position.
The Lao People's Revolutionary Party had ruled without a constitution since 1975; one was finally promulgated in 1991. Stability 58 is a durable regime in an undemanding country, not a popular one.
separatism 0.09 is the Hmong insurgency in Xaisomboun, a remnant of the CIA's Secret Army that was still being fought in 1990.
Military index 2: about 55,000 under arms, no capacity beyond internal security.
